answer: Sequential work attestation. Each identity must publish a pearl of verifiable compute: a hash chain whose links are released only after real elapsed wall-clock time, checked against a public clock. A single operator running N identities must serialize that work on one machine, so per-identity cost is N times the real latency. The chain is inspected through a prism of independent timestamps, and any identity whose timing overlaps another from the same operator is flagged like tracks in tundra snow. Faking parallelism requires N separate physical clocks, a hard cost per identity.
